items.content_html:
🛠️ HyperCard to HTML Converter

Summary
The HyperCard to HTML Converter turns HyperCard 2.x stacks into standalone HTML files that run directly in modern web browsers. It was built to recover and share early 1990s stacks previously trapped on old floppy disk images.

Why it’s interesting
It allows 30-year-old legacy HyperCard stacks to run again in modern browsers and is open-source under the MIT license.

Target user
People with old HyperCard files looking to convert and run them in modern web browsers.

items.content_html:
🛠️ Minilith – A zero-dependency CMS stored inside a PNG file

Summary
Minilith is a zero-dependency database-free content management system where the entire state, including posts, pages, and settings, is compressed and stored inside the pixels of a PNG file using steganography. It relies on browser APIs to compress, secure, and render a micro blog directly from the image.

Why it’s interesting
It uses steganography to store an entire CMS and its database directly inside the pixels of a PNG file with zero external dependencies.
